## Natural history notes

A tiny oak gall wasp characterized less by the adult insect than by the swollen stem galls it induces on southern live oak. In Florida, the Southern Live Oak Stem Gall Wasp is associated with live oak, especially in hammocks, oak woods, parks, yards, and forest edges where mature live oaks occur; it has also been documented in southern Florida gall communities. The larva develops protected inside the woody gall, using oak tissue for food and shelter, while the gall itself can support a broader community of parasitoids, inquilines, and other gall-associated insects.
